belongs_to: Opening text: 'Triangles come in various shapes. Some of them are shown below.' (naming of triangles by their vertices)
description: One row of FOUR separate triangles printed side by side, each a plain black outline (no shading, no tick marks, no side lengths, no angle marks). Vertex letters stand just outside the corners and the name of each triangle is printed centred under it. (1) Tall narrow scalene triangle: A at the top apex (slightly right of the left side), B at the bottom-left corner, C at the bottom-right corner (C a little lower than B). Name under it: 'Δ ABC'. (2) Wide triangle with a horizontal base: Y at the left end of the base, Z at the right end of the base, X at the apex above the middle of the base (slightly right of centre). Name under the base: 'Δ YZX'. (3) Tilted triangle: U at the top apex, V at the bottom-left corner, W at the bottom-right corner (W a little higher than V). Name under it: 'ΔWUV'. (4) Tall tilted triangle: B at the top apex, A at the left corner (about three-quarters of the way down), U at the bottom-right corner (the lowest corner). Name under it: 'ΔBAU'. The four triangles are different shapes; the names show vertices listed in any order (YZX, WUV, BAU).
unclear: Exact side lengths and angle sizes are not given (figure is only for naming).

belongs_to: Text 'Say we draw the base AB of length 4 cm (see the figure below), and mark the third point C using a ruler such that AC = 4 cm' (ruler-only trial method)
description: Triangle ABC drawn upright: A at the bottom-left, B at the bottom-right, C at the top (apex above and slightly to the right of A). AB is a solid horizontal line with the label '4 cm' centred under it. AC is a solid line with the label '4 cm' written along it (rotated, on its left side). BC is a DASHED line with the label '4 cm?' written along it (rotated, on its right side), showing the length is still to be checked. Letters: C above the apex, A at the left of the bottom-left corner, B at the right of the bottom-right corner. As drawn BC is visibly longer than AC and AB (about 1.2 times), so the triangle is not equilateral.

belongs_to: Step 1: 'Using a compass, construct a sufficiently long arc of radius 4 cm from A, as shown in the figure. The point C is somewhere on this arc.'
description: A full circle of radius 4 cm with centre A, drawn as a DASHED circle except for one solid arc. A is a solid dot at the centre (label 'A' at its lower-left). A solid horizontal segment (the radius AB) runs from A to the right end of the circle; B is the point where it meets the circle (label 'B' just right of that end, small vertical tick at the end), and the label '4 cm' is centred under the segment. Only the upper-right part of the circle is solid: from the very top point of the circle clockwise down to a point about 23 degrees above the horizontal on the right (an arc of about 65 degrees, upper-right). Everything else on the circle is dashed. No point C is marked.

belongs_to: Step 2: 'Construct another arc of radius 4 cm from B.' (the picture shows both circles, centres A and B)
description: Two equal DASHED circles of radius 4 cm: one centred at A (it passes through B), one centred at B (it passes through A). A (left) and B (right) are solid dots joined by a solid horizontal segment AB with the label '4 cm' centred under it; 'A' is written at the lower-left of its dot, 'B' at the right of its dot. The circles cross at two points, one directly above the middle of AB and one directly below it (unlabelled). Two short SOLID arcs are drawn at the top: one is a part of A's circle from the top point of A's circle curving down on its right side to a point above B; the other is a part of B's circle from the top point of B's circle curving down on its left side to a point above A. The two solid arcs cross each other at the upper intersection point of the circles. All the rest of both circles is dashed.

belongs_to: Step 3: 'Join AC and BC to get the required equilateral triangle.' (C = the point of intersection of the arcs)
description: Same drawing as the Step 2 picture (two equal dashed circles of radius 4 cm centred at A and at B, the same two short solid arcs at the top, solid base AB labelled '4 cm' under it, A at lower-left of its dot and B at right of its dot) with the upper point where the two arcs cross now labelled 'C' (letter just above-left of the point). Two straight solid lines AC and BC are added from A to C and from B to C, completing the equilateral triangle ABC with AB horizontal at the bottom and C at the top. The lower intersection point of the circles is unlabelled.

belongs_to: Figure it Out Q2: 'Use the points on the circles and/or their centres to form isosceles and equilateral triangles. The circles are of the same size.' (left figure)
description: Two circles of the SAME size, overlapping, drawn side by side horizontally (solid outlines). Their centres A (left) and B (right) are marked with solid dots with the letters 'A' just left of its dot and 'B' just right of its dot. The distance between the centres equals the radius, so A lies on the circle centred at B and B lies on the circle centred at A, and the circles overlap in a lens shape in the middle. No segments are drawn. Caption printed below: 'A and B are the centres of circles of the same size'.

belongs_to: Figure it Out Q2: 'Use the points on the circles and/or their centres to form isosceles and equilateral triangles. The circles are of the same size.' (right figure)
description: Three circles of the SAME size (solid outlines) overlapping each other. Their centres are solid dots: A at the upper left (letter 'A' at its left), B at the upper right (letter 'B' at its right) on the same horizontal level, and C below the middle of AB (letter 'C' below its dot). The three centres are the corners of an equilateral triangle whose side equals the radius, so each centre lies on the other two circles. The two upper circles overlap in a lens, and the lower circle (centre C) passes through A and B. No segments are drawn. Caption printed below: 'A, B, and C are the centres of circles of the same size'.

belongs_to: Triangle Inequality text: 'a small plot of plain land having a tent, a tree, and a pole... (i) the straight-line path to the tree (the red path) or (ii) the straight-line path from the tent to the pole, followed by the straight-line path from the pole to the tree (the yellow path)'
description: Coloured illustration on a light-blue rounded patch. A tall palm tree stands at the left (its base at the lower left); a tent (beige, triangular) stands at the right (its entrance at the lower right); two cartoon children stand behind/right near the tent (decoration). A thin vertical pole stands in the middle with its foot at the top corner of the yellow path. A RED straight line runs horizontally along the ground from the foot of the tree to the entrance of the tent (the direct path). A YELLOW path of two straight lines: from the tent entrance up and to the left to the foot of the pole, then from the pole down and to the left to the foot of the tree (the roundabout path). The red line and the two yellow lines together form a triangle (red base at the bottom, yellow apex at the pole); the two yellow sides are clearly longer than the red side combined. No lengths or letters written.
unclear: The children, tree, tent are illustration; the mathematical content is the red segment and the two yellow segments (a triangle with the pole at the apex).

belongs_to: 'Visualising the construction of circles': 'Let AB be the base of length 8 cm... Suppose we construct a circle of radius 4 cm with A as the centre.'

belongs_to: 'Case 2: Circles do not intersect internally... sum of the two radii < AB' (figure below the formula)

belongs_to: 'Case 3: Circles intersect each other. AB is composed of one radius and a part of the other. So, sum of the two radii > AB'
description: Two solid circles that overlap in a lens: a smaller circle on the left with centre A and a larger circle on the right with centre B (radius of A about 0.58 times radius of B). A and B are bold solid dots with letters 'A' just left of A and 'B' just right of B, joined by a solid horizontal segment AB. Radius marks: a double-headed grey arrow labelled 'radius 1' runs horizontally above AB from a dashed vertical line through A to a dashed vertical line at the right edge of A's circle (on AB); a double-headed grey arrow labelled 'radius 2' runs horizontally below AB from a dashed vertical line at the left edge of B's circle (on AB) to a dashed vertical line through B. The right edge of the small circle on AB lies to the right of the left edge of the big circle, so the two radius marks overlap over the lens-shaped part; AB is thus one radius (radius 1) plus part of the other. No numbers are written.

belongs_to: Worked example (Steps 1 to 3): 'Draw the base AB of length 5 cm. Draw ∠A and ∠B of measures 45° and 80° respectively. The point of intersection of the two new line segments is the third vertex C.'
